I'd say that this is a widely different story in comparison to SCP-445-EX, even if they both do contain the same base element. This focuses more on the humor and bizarre nature of dado having a laundry and tan shop run by normal people, while 445-EX focuses on depicting how Wondertainment changes their activities after many years, with an emotional and realistic focus. Both of them focus on the unique aspects of their respective groups and tell a story heavily tied to the group. Focusing only on the surface level element of "a GoI but public" does a disservice to both articles.

Neither article really discards the iconic aspects of their group to appear quirky, but rather use those aspects to tell a different kind of story heavily reliant on the fact that those groups specifically are the focus.

item.content:encoded:
I'm loathe to say that people shouldn't do a thing just because it's already been done before, but I'm prone to agree — character-jokes like dado work best in small doses. And the more we learn about dado, the less fun dado becomes.

Indiana Jones is a cool hat Harrison Ford wears while he punches Nazis. Dado is a broken keyboard someone types on while they produce magic pills based on hilarious misunderstandings. Both of these ideas operate on a 'less-is-more' principle: Exploring them too deeply risks destroying the magic and the charm.

ETA: Not to say this article is bad, or the tipping point; I don't honestly know? But I definitely feel like the tipping point is approaching.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
So my main problem with this is I don't think it would be classified at all. They wouldn't have given it a designation straight up just because of a potential connection to dado, which means it makes no sense to me for it to be Explained (because they never actually determined it was anomalous before hand.) Obviously the incidents with the billboards was anomalous, so I kind of feel like that should have been the actual target of the article rather than the laundry itself.

My headcanon for the Foundation is and has always been "utterly paranoid." They tend to err on the side of caution and jump the gun, and in this case "anomalously advertised" and "known PoI is owner" was enough for them to tentatively give it an SCP designation while investigating. There's no real harm in doing that, and you don't have to transfer from some other format to an SCP if it does end up being anomalous.

The other thing is just how free this agent is throwing around information to the random civilian that, for all they know, is working directly for (or could even BE) dado.

That's fair, and I've reworked what he says a little to try and lessen that.

item.title: tan and laundry by dado
item.content:encoded:
In waste management by dado, dado mentions that he runs a laundry and tan service. I have decided to write that, the joke being that there is nothing anomalous about dado's laundry. He's a brilliant entrepreneur and true capitalist who dabbles in washing machines, anomalous drugs and tanning beds. (But not anomalaundry)

NOTE: The second sentence the Receptionist says is a question that ends in a period. This is an intentional stylistic choice to convey the apathy of the Receptionist, not an error.
